title: Cross-language function schema validation and invocation helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a set of language-idiomatic helper utilities for function/tool calling across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Work includes JSON Schema-based input validation, lightweight invocation wrappers that handle sync/async and streaming responses, deterministic retry semantics for idempotent functions, and consistent example snippets for developer docs. Goal: reduce integration errors, provide clear failure modes, and improve ergonomics for streaming function outputs and incremental parsing.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a function validator that accepts a JSON Schema and returns clear typed errors for missing/extra fields
Invocation helper wraps underlying API call and normalizes response shapes across sync/async/streaming modes
Retry policy implemented with backoff and idempotency checks; documented default for non-idempotent functions
End-to-end examples added to SDK repos and developer docs for Python, TypeScript, and Go
Unit and integration tests cover schema edge cases, streaming chunk ordering, and retry scenarios
implementation_notes: Design: use a compact schema subset to avoid shipping a heavy validator in the browser TS bundle. Python: use jsonschema with a small wrapper to map errors to user-friendly messages and typed dataclasses for invocation. TS: runtime checks via a generated lightweight validator (ajv-lite pattern) to produce stable error codes. Go: compile-time struct tags plus a small runtime check for unknown fields. Invocation helper responsibility: validate input, attach idempotency token when appropriate, call Redwood API, expose streaming iterator/async generator, and surface clear retryable vs non-retryable errors.
testing_plan: Unit: validator negative/positive cases per language. Streaming: simulate chunk reordering and partial failures using a mock server. Retry: simulate transient 5xx and connection errors and assert backoff/resume behavior. Integration: sample app that uses tool calling with a function that produces incremental data, assert SDK consumer sees identical sequence across Python/TS/Go. Add fuzz tests for schema coercion edge cases.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge language SDK PRs behind feature flags. 2) Publish pre-release packages and run customer beta (selected internal apps). 3) Gradual enablement for new function-calling requests with opt-in flag for one week. 4) Monitor errors/latency in Console and rollback if regression >2% error rate. 5) Flip default after 2 weeks if stable.
